parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both services deal with appointments, so the concern is roughly the same. The problem is that the two files use different abstractions. SchedulingService reaches data through purpose-built DAOs (PatientDao, AppointmentDao), turns the rows into domain entities (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment), keeps rules on those entities (overlaps, cancel, isMinor, treatsMinors) and reports failures with the domain error SchedulingError. VisitNotesService skips all of that. It takes the raw PrismaService client, queries prisma.visitNote directly, builds row ids and timestamps itself, and returns a loose VisitNote interface declared in the service file instead of a business entity. It never checks that the appointment exists and never uses SchedulingError, so how notes relate to appointments is not enforced the way the rest of the module enforces its rules. This is a bypass of the module's own data-access and entity abstractions, not an import-direction issue, so the rubric's 'bypass the module's own abstractions' failure applies.

violations.message: Bypasses the module's abstractions. SchedulingService uses DAOs (PatientDao/AppointmentDao), domain entities and SchedulingError. VisitNotesService queries PrismaService.visitNote directly, builds ids and timestamps inline, and returns an ad-hoc VisitNote interface instead of an entity, so the module mixes two different data-access and modelling styles.
